headline_ea_first: Expert & Authority builds the name. AI for Founders builds the machine.
intro: They live on different pathways (Expert & Authority in Authority, AI for Founders in Entrepreneurship), but both are co-led by Vishen and both sell to overlapping lists, so the line between them has to be stated once, precisely, and held. It is not a difference of topic. It is a difference of what is broken in the student's business.

ea.name: Expert & Authority Mastery
ea.pain: "I'm great at what I do, but nobody knows me."
ea.diagnosis: They already know something valuable. The problem is that nobody is buying it yet: no profile, no offer, no path from stranger to client. Seventeen weeks building a name and a ladder for it to climb.
ea.outcome: your expertise, earning. A niche only you could own, a product live on the internet, strangers finding you weekly, and a ladder that carries someone from a free download to a five-figure relationship
ea.proof: assets published and first revenue banked
ea.artefact: Your Ladder, Live: an edge, a published product, a masterclass shot, a traffic tap running, three paid rungs

Labs led by Alessio Pieroni, Kash Rupalia, Jimmy Naraine, Sabrina Stocker and Safwaan Mohammed (in consideration)

aif.name: AI for Founders Mastery
aif.pain: "My business can't run a single day without me."
aif.diagnosis: They already have something to sell. The problem is that every part of it runs through them. Eighteen weeks rebuilding five pillars (marketing, sales, operations, people, finance) as AI systems that run while they lead.
aif.outcome: a business that grows without grinding you down. Leads arriving, nothing going cold, delivery running itself, the numbers talking to you, and your Fridays back
aif.artefact: the Founder Operating System: company brain, demand engine, delivery agents, finance cockpit
aif.led_by: Vishen Lakhiani + Daniel Priestley as co-owners, with Noelle Russell, Marie Forleo and Shawn Kanungo in consideration; implementation labs by Vykintas Glodenis with Alex Dogliotti. Academy roster options: Nick Sonnenberg, Cassie Kozyrkov, Domenic Ashburn, Sara Davison & Tyler Fisk

router.question: "Do you have something to sell that's drowning you, or something to say that nobody's paying for yet?"
router.answer: Drowning in delivery → AI for Founders. Unknown with real expertise → Expert & Authority. Can't hold a room at all → Speaking & Influence. If a prospect can't answer, they are Expert & Authority: you cannot systematise demand that doesn't exist yet. The usual sequence is Expert & Authority first, then AI for Founders. Build the name, then the machine to serve it.

overlap_rules: Content: AI for Founders automates the pipeline; Expert & Authority finds the voice that goes into it. Offers: AI for Founders prices and delivers what exists; Expert & Authority designs the ladder that doesn't exist yet. Demand: AI for Founders builds the capture mechanism; Expert & Authority builds the reason anyone fills it in. Neither programme teaches the other's half, and the zero-overlap faculty enforces it.
retention: S&I's own detractors flagged scope drift, verbatim: "I'm only interested in speaking, not creating a course or teaching or creating a business" — on the week that programme drifted into Expert & Authority territory. Scope drift is not a marketing problem; it is a refund generator. Each programme teaches its own promise and cross-refers the rest. The sequence also matches our intake: 68% female, 78% aged 45+, service businesses built on expertise, and 91% of Social Media Mastery students not yet earning from their audience. Those students have nothing to systematise yet.
